YouTube · @hotcoinglobal · audit as of 13 Oct 2026

Hotcoin YouTube Reset

The channel needs fewer uploads, one clear reason to watch, and two long series people can put on while they eat.

Scope: channel audit, long-form series, thumbnails, postingGoal: views, not revenue
The short version
  1. The channel is flooded with clips nobody chose to watch. 14 TOKEN2049 clips went up in 6 days and earned 28 views between them. They now cover the top of the Videos tab, so they are the first thing a visitor sees.
  2. Hotcoin 101 is in a format YouTube has nowhere to show. The episodes are horizontal and about 60 seconds long. That is too short for the long-form feed, and horizontal video can't go into the Shorts feed.
  3. Educational and story content beats brand content about 3 to 1. The older educational Shorts have a median of 87 views. The newest 50 brand and campaign Shorts have a median of 28.
  4. The fix: launch two long-form series, Bubble Files (money history) and Price Tag (the economics of everyday things), plus a Sunday 101 compilation. The Tulip Mania 101 already shows the style works.

3. The long-form series

Brief: broad, recognisable, something people put on while eating. That is lean-back viewing, often on a TV, so the episodes are 10–14 minute stories with large on-screen type, chapters, and a narrator who does most of the work. Both series sit next to what Hotcoin sells (crypto, gold, US stocks) without being about Hotcoin. Each episode ends with a 20-second lesson in the 101 style, then a tease for the next episode.

Series A · Bubble Files

Famous manias, crashes, heists and frauds, told as stories. This genre already does well on YouTube (Magnates Media, Patrick Boyle, Bloomberg Originals). The Tulip Mania 101 is a ready pilot, and it already uses the paper "case file" look, so the two series feel related. Every story carries a trading lesson (leverage, position sizing, custody), so the brand fit comes from the story itself.

Fact-check every figure in titles and thumbnails just before publishing. Prices and rankings (World Cup costs, Nvidia vs countries) change, so the slate leaves those numbers open on purpose.

Series C · Hotcoin 101, Sunday edition

Five 101 episodes stitched into one 8–10 minute video, for example "Crypto in 10 Minutes: Blockchains, Exchanges, Candles and Slang", with chapters. It costs almost nothing to make, gives the existing 101s a long-form home, and gets search traffic for beginner questions.

Episode shape (Bubble Files and Price Tag)

TimePartWhat happens
0:00Cold openStart in the middle of the most dramatic moment. No logo, no intro.
0:30The questionOne line that makes the viewer need the answer: "How does a flower end up worth a house?"
1:00Act 1: setupThe world, the people, the money
4:00Act 2: the maniaThe climb, told with charts and archive images
8:00Act 3: the breakThe crash or the twist
11:00The lesson20 seconds in the 101 file style, then a soft Hotcoin mention
11:30Next timeTease the next episode, with an end screen linking to it

4. Thumbnails

The model is Johnny Harris: the host's face showing how the story feels, one real photo, one data graphic (a map or a price chart) with hand-drawn red marks, and a headline of four words at most that says exactly what happened. Here are the first three, rendered at full size from the host photos:

The same three at real phone size, 168 px wide:

The rules behind them

  • Face: the expression matches the story. Shock for a crash, thinking for a puzzle, a side glance toward the map.
  • Headline: four words at most, and it names who or what. White condensed type, with the key words in a red box.
  • One graphic built from real data: a price chart or a map, with a hand-drawn red circle on the point that matters.
  • Proof line: a small tag bottom left with the fact behind the headline (Texas 1979–80, record $4.41/lb, 1,000+ tonnes a year).
  • Use Studio's Test & Compare on every long video: upload 3 thumbnails (and 3 titles if your channel has the option) and YouTube picks the winner by watch time. Availability varies by channel, so check under the video's Thumbnail section in Studio.
  • Claude renders every thumbnail from one template in the repo (youtube/thumbs/thumb.html), so swapping the expression, photo or headline takes one line, and each video can ship with 3 variants.

Research and scriptClaude
Sourced script with a fact list and timing, about 1,600 words for 11 minutes. You approve it.
VoiceoverTeam
One consistent human narrator, about 20 minutes of recording per episode. This matters most for quality: a synthetic voice over 12 minutes loses people, and YouTube is pushing back on mass-produced AI channels. The repo's Kokoro voice is fine for draft cuts.
EditClaude
Remotion, the same pipeline as the 101s and Uptober: archive images (credited in FOOTAGE_CREDITS), charts, maps, and the file-style typography.
Thumbnail ×3 and a Short trailerClaude
Rendered from the episode itself.
ScheduleClaude
Uploaded as a scheduled draft with title, description, chapters, tags and thumbnail. You approve it before it goes live.
